thread.title: Apple’s stock bounces back in face of Goldman’s lowered outlook

author: Tomi Kilgore
title: Apple’s stock bounces back in face of Goldman’s lowered outlook
text:
Shares of Apple Inc. bounced Tuesday, to defy a downbeat report from Goldman Sachs in which analyst Rod Hall cut his price target and earnings outlook on concerns over “deteriorating” iPhone demand.
The technology giant’s stock AAPL, +0.16% fell as much as 1.4% to a 3 1/2-month low earlier in the session, before recovering to gain 0.9% in midday trade. If the gain holds, it would snap a three-session losing streak that shaved 7.5% off the price.
Goldman’s Hall slashed his price target to $209, which was nearly 7% above current levels, from $240. He also lowered his fiscal 2019 earnings estimate to $13.00 a share from $13.44, his revenue forecast to $269.9 billion from $279.7 billion and his iPhone unit projection to 202.9 million from 214.8 million. He reiterated the neutral rating he’s had on Apple since Feb. 6.
Don’t miss : Apple stock sinks as concerns over slowing iPhone demand take hold .
Hall said his reductions follow the profit and revenue warning from Apple supplier Lumentum Holdings Inc. LITE, +5.95% on Monday, with Lumentum blaming one of its largest customers for requesting a material reduction in shipments in laser diodes for 3-D sensing. Although Lumentum didn’t say that customer was Apple, it has disclosed in the past that Apple was its largest customer, and a number of analysts have assumed it was Apple.
Apple didn’t respond to a request for comment.
On Tuesday, Qorvo Inc. QRVO, -1.00% cut its fiscal third-quarter revenue guidance range to $800 million to $840 million from $880 million to $900 million, and lowered its adjusted EPS outlook to $1.70 at the midpoint from $1.95 at the midpoint, citing “demand changes for flagship smartphones.” Although the company didn’t name Apple as the reason for the warning, it said in its annual report for fiscal 2018 that Apple was its largest end customer, accounting for 36% of total revenue.
Given the extent of Lumentum’s warning, Hall said he infers the likely customer was Apple, and raises concerns that end-market demand for new iPhone models is deteriorating. It also follows Apple’s downbeat outlook for the holiday period that tainted an otherwise better-than-expected earnings report.
Also read : Opinion: When the going gets tough, Apple hides its numbers .
“While Apple may have already contemplated some weakness in its guidance, we feel the timing and magnitude of the [Lumentum] reduction suggests Apple is seeing incrementally worse demand data,” Hall wrote in a note to clients.
“We note this could easily right itself given the bulk of demand comes in late December but we feel more prudent sell through forecasts are warranted due to the timing and magnitude of this warning,” he wrote.
Apple shares have shed 6.2% over the past three months, but has still gained 16% year to date, In comparison, the technology-heavy Nasdaq 100 index NDX, +0.90% has lost 6.5% the past three months and the Dow Jones Industrial Average DJIA, +0.10% of which Apple is a component, has gained 1.1%.
